reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that sentiment propagates across a network of companies based on shared news mentions. The network is constructed using cosine similarity of news coverage vectors, which reflects how often two entities appear together in articles. This network is then analyzed using Louvain modularity to detect clusters of related companies. Entity-level sentiment is computed per article and aggregated per company over time. These sentiment dynamics are linked to market outcomes via cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) around sentiment shock events. The mathematical framework relies on graph theory (networks), signal processing (cosine similarity), and statistics (Mann–Whitney U tests). The failure mode arises when news co-occurrence does not reflect true economic relationships or when sentiment scores are noisy. The model assumes that sentiment shocks are exogenous and that market responses can be captured through event studies.
